item1.head: Michel B. raises their voice in the Monday team meetings.
item1.text: From March to June, six witnesses describe department meetings where the head of department goes over the week’s instructions in a curt tone, cuts people off and publicly criticises the work handed in. Two of them say they stopped speaking up there.
item1.quote: “The Monday meetings have been different since they arrived. We just wait for it to be over.”

item2.head: Michel B. reprimands a colleague in front of the whole team.
item2.text: On 2 April, in a department meeting, an officer who was asking for extra time was told in front of everyone that their work was not up to the expected standard. Two witnesses report the scene in the same terms; none of the managers present intervened.
item2.quote: “They said it in front of everyone. Nobody reacted, and we moved on to the next item.”

outro.title: The sorting is done. The investigation is yours to lead.
outro.text: The software prepares the ground: it masks, it files, it dates, it sources. Interpretation, the debrief and the conclusion are not its business.

ai.title: AI spots, dates and labels. It does not conclude for you.
ai.lede: Generating text on your behalf holds no interest for us, and letting an algorithm decide what your conclusions should be even less. Our tools exist to give you as much grip as possible on your testimonies: anonymising them, filing them, dating them, sourcing them. What to make of them remains your profession.

meta.title: Cohortes — open testimony platform for groups at work
meta.description: Cohortes’ open testimony platform: everyone files their testimony whenever they want, the group decides what it follows, and sees what keeps coming back over the year.

hero.title: Making a group visible to itself.
hero.lede: Everyone files their testimony whenever they want. The group makes them its own, asks its own questions, and sees what keeps coming back week after week.

principle.title: The principle
principle.text: In an organisation, everyone knows their own situation. Nobody knows how many others are living the same one. The platform gathers testimonies over the year and shows what keeps coming back — it is the group that decides what it wants to follow, not a set of indicators chosen elsewhere.

s1.title: Forming a group
s1.text: Members come together in small groups: by occupation, by seniority, by gender or by level in the hierarchy. It is these groups that give testimony.

s2.title: Giving testimony
s2.text: Everyone files their testimony whenever they want, while the experience is still fresh. Anonymised, the testimonies are read and discussed by the other members of the group.

s3.title: Asking
s3.text: The group asks its own questions — up to five, persistent. They become its indicators: what it has decided to keep an eye on.

s4.title: Understanding
s4.text: Each week, the testimonies filed are summarised and set against the group’s questions. Recurring themes appear, and how they shift over time with them.

s5.title: Deciding
s5.text: Equipped with its own testimonies and its own questions, the group decides. Over the months, a memory builds up of what has been said, seen and changed.

a.q: What support measures have been put in place?
a.a: Three testimonies mention the September training, two the presence of a designated contact. Nobody mentions the discussion sessions announced in June.

b.q: How is the arrival of the new software changing our autonomy?
b.a: The subject comes back for the fifth week running, this time from the angle of imposed deadlines rather than the tool itself.

status.title: Where this product stands
status.text: The platform exists but is no longer sold self-service. We prefer to move forward case by case, and to build a platform suited to the needs of each organisation that wants to use it seriously.
status.more: Why we made that choice, and what we learned from selling it, is told on the about page.

hero.title: We work on one thing only: making a group visible to itself.

origin.title: Where it comes from
origin.a: From the retrospective. It is a workshop borrowed from agile methods: every two weeks, the people who work together stop for an hour and say what worked, what got stuck, what ought to change.
origin.b: Two things frustrated us. The first: once the workshop is over, what was said is hard to consult again. Rereading it, cross-checking it or counting it takes work that we do not always make time for.
origin.c: The second: follow-up hangs by a thread. The actions decided are usually written down, but knowing whether the problem raised in March is still there in June, or how many times it has come back since, in fact rests on the memory of those who were in the room.
origin.d: That said, the retrospective has one merit: it builds a team. By saying together what is going well and what is not, people who work side by side become a group.
origin.e: Hence the idea: a platform where everyone files their testimony whenever they want, and where the group decides for itself what it wants to follow. The starting hypothesis came down to one question: if a group takes hold of a testimony tool, does that change the way work is organised?

market.title: The reality of the market
market.a: The first obstacle was the fear of free text. A platform where any subject can be discussed is unsettling: you do not know what will be written there, nor what you will have to do about it.
market.b: The second runs deeper. Quality of working life is still a byword for emergency, rarely for foresight: people call once something has already broken, not to stop it breaking.
market.c: After a year and a half, the conclusion was simple: change or shut down. It was AD Conseil, an occupational psychology practice, that opened the other door for us, the one to workplace harassment investigations.

a.title: The tool prepares, you conclude
a.text: It anonymises, labels, dates and sources. Interpretation, the debrief and the conclusion remain your profession.

b.title: Nothing is asserted without its source
b.text: Every fact is dated and tied back to the testimony it was drawn from. That is what makes a debrief defensible.

c.title: The coding framework is yours
c.text: Shipped with the software, built from the themes that surface from the testimonies, or created by hand. Three routes, a single grid: yours.

a.title: Speech should travel up, not down
a.text: Workplace listening tools are top-down: management asks the questions, employees tick the boxes. Here, it is the ground that says what counts, in its own words.

b.title: The group before the individual
b.text: What is interesting is not who is speaking, but how a group stands in relation to the way work is organised. An isolated testimony reads as a feeling; a body of them tells the story of a system.

c.title: A questionnaire only finds what it is looking for
c.text: Closed questions put bounds on the answers. Open testimony lets through what nobody had thought to ask about.
